From 15930da42f8981dc42c19038042947b475b19f47 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2024 18:55:55 -1000
Subject: [PATCH] workqueue: Don't call cpumask_test_cpu() with -1 CPU in
 wq_update_node_max_active()

For wq_update_node_max_active(), @off_cpu of -1 indicates that no CPU is
going down. The function was incorrectly calling cpumask_test_cpu() with -1
CPU leading to oopses like the following on some archs:

  Unable to handle kernel paging request at virtual address ffff0002100296e0
  ..
  pc : wq_update_node_max_active+0x50/0x1fc
  lr : wq_update_node_max_active+0x1f0/0x1fc
  ...
  Call trace:
    wq_update_node_max_active+0x50/0x1fc
    apply_wqattrs_commit+0xf0/0x114
    apply_workqueue_attrs_locked+0x58/0xa0
    alloc_workqueue+0x5ac/0x774
    workqueue_init_early+0x460/0x540
    start_kernel+0x258/0x684
    __primary_switched+0xb8/0xc0
  Code: 9100a273 35000d01 53067f00 d0016dc1 (f8607a60)
  
diff --git a/kernel/workqueue.c b/kernel/workqueue.c
index 9221a4c57ae1..31c1373505d8 100644
--- a/kernel/workqueue.c
+++ b/kernel/workqueue.c
@@ -1510,7 +1510,7 @@ static void wq_update_node_max_active(struct workqueue_struct *wq, int off_cpu)
 
 	lockdep_assert_held(&wq->mutex);
 
-	if (!cpumask_test_cpu(off_cpu, effective))
+	if (off_cpu >= 0 && !cpumask_test_cpu(off_cpu, effective))
 		off_cpu = -1;
 
 	total_cpus = cpumask_weight_and(effective, cpu_online_mask);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/workqueue.c`**
- The condition in the `wq_update_node_max_active` function was modified. The original line:
  ```c
  if (!cpumask_test_cpu(off_cpu, effective))
  ```
  was changed to:
  ```c
  if (off_cpu >= 0 && !cpumask_test_cpu(off_cpu, effective))
  ```
- This change ensures that `cpumask_test_cpu()` is only called if `off_cpu` is not -1, preventing potential kernel crashes when -1 is passed as an argument.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug where passing -1 to `cpumask_test_cpu()` could lead to kernel paging requests and crashes on certain architectures. By adding the check for `off_cpu >= 0`, the patch prevents the function from executing the test with an invalid CPU index, thereby enhancing the stability of the workqueue functionality in the kernel.

Signed-off-by: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Reported-by: Marek Szyprowski <m.szyprowski@samsung.com>
Reported-by: Nathan Chancellor <nathan@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Nathan Chancellor <nathan@kernel.org>
Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/91eacde0-df99-4d5c-a980-91046f66e612@samsung.com
Fixes: 5797b1c18919 ("workqueue: Implement system-wide nr_active enforcement for unbound workqueues")

Here is the root cause:
The bug occurs because the function `wq_update_node_max_active()` incorrectly calls `cpumask_test_cpu()` with an invalid CPU index of -1, which is not a valid CPU identifier. This leads to kernel paging requests and crashes on certain architectures when the function attempts to access memory using this invalid index.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static void wq_update_node_max_active(struct workqueue_struct *wq, int off_cpu)
 {
 	struct cpumask *effective = unbound_effective_cpumask(wq);
 	int min_active = READ_ONCE(wq->min_active);
 	int max_active = READ_ONCE(wq->max_active);
 	int total_cpus, node;
 
 	lockdep_assert_held(&wq->mutex);
 
-	if (!cpumask_test_cpu(off_cpu, effective))
+	if (off_cpu >= 0 && !cpumask_test_cpu(off_cpu, effective))
 		off_cpu = -1;
 
 	total_cpus = cpumask_weight_and(effective, cpu_online_mask);
 	if (off_cpu >= 0)
 		total_cpus--;
 
 	for_each_node(node) {
 		int node_cpus;
 
 		node_cpus = cpumask_weight_and(effective, cpumask_of_node(node));
 		if (off_cpu >= 0 && cpu_to_node(off_cpu) == node)
 			node_cpus--;
 
 		wq_node_nr_active(wq, node)->max =
 			clamp(DIV_ROUND_UP(max_active * node_cpus, total_cpus),
 			      min_active, max_active);
 	}
 
 	wq_node_nr_active(wq, NUMA_NO_NODE)->max = min_active;
 }
